title: "Repository access control model"
order: 8

## Overview

This page describes who can read and write the repositories that hold TAF code, introduced in the [business architecture](business.qmd). There are three types of repository:

- **National Estimation (NE)**: the data of one country, as estimated by its national estimators.
- **Stock Coordination (SC)**: the data of one stock, as brought together by its stock coordinator.
- **Stock Assessment (SA)**: the assessment of one stock.

The repositories form a tree: the NE repositories of the countries that contribute data to a stock feed its SC repository, which in turn feeds its SA repository (see [Data flow between repositories](#data-flow-between-repositories)).

Access rights are derived from a combination of:

- Claims assigned to users
- Working Group (WG) membership
- Advice Drafting Group (ADG) membership
- Advisory Committee (ACOM) membership
- ICES staff membership
- The NE repositories that contribute data to each SC repository

The authoritative data sources for these relationships are:

| Information | Source system |
|-------------|---------------|
| User → NE country claims | RDBES |
| User → SC stock claims | SID |
| User → SA stock claims | SID |
| Stock → WG mapping | SID |
| Stock → ADG mapping | SID |
| User → WG membership | CRM |
| User → ADG membership | CRM |
| User → ACOM membership | CRM |
| NE repository → SC repository contributions | Contributor table |
| ICES staff membership | Identity / HR source |

Where:

- **RDBES** is the ICES Regional Database and Estimation System.
- **SID** is the ICES Stock Information Database.
- **CRM** is the ICES contact and membership system, which records who belongs to each group.

## Repository types

Each repository type is identified by one attribute:

| Repository type | Attribute |
|-----------------|-----------|
| NE | Country |
| SC | Stock code |
| SA | Stock code |

Examples:

| Repository | Attribute |
|------------|-----------|
| NE-DK | country = DK |
| SC-cod.27.347d | stock = cod.27.347d |
| SA-cod.27.347d | stock = cod.27.347d |

## Write access

Users receive write access through explicit claims.

| Claim type | Claim value | Write access |
|------------|-------------|--------------|
| NE | DK | NE repositories with country = DK |
| SC | cod.27.347d | SC repositories with stock = cod.27.347d |
| SA | cod.27.347d | SA repositories with stock = cod.27.347d |

### Write access model

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR

C["Claim
Type + Value"]

R["Repository
Type + Attribute"]

C --> M{"Match?"}
R --> M

M -->|NE & country equal| W1["Write"]
M -->|SC & stock equal| W2["Write"]
M -->|SA & stock equal| W3["Write"]
```

## Read access

Read access is determined from a combination of global permissions, group membership, stock ownership and the flow of data between repositories.

### Global read access

The following users can read all repositories:

- ICES staff
- ACOM members

ACOM membership is maintained in CRM.

### Working Groups (WG)

Each stock is assigned to a Working Group (WG), for example:

```text
cod.27.347d → WGNSSK
```

Members of a WG can read:

- All SC repositories for stocks assigned to that WG
- All SA repositories for stocks assigned to that WG
- All NE repositories that contribute data to those SC repositories

WG membership is maintained in CRM. Stock-to-WG mappings are maintained in SID.

### Advice Drafting Groups (ADG)

Each stock is also assigned to an Advice Drafting Group (ADG).

Members of an ADG can read:

- All SC repositories for stocks assigned to that ADG
- All SA repositories for stocks assigned to that ADG
- All NE repositories that contribute data to those SC repositories

ADG membership is maintained in CRM. Stock-to-ADG mappings are maintained in SID.

### Data flow between repositories

Data flow from NE repositories to SC repositories, and from SC repositories to SA repositories. Each NE repository contributes the data of one country to the SC repositories of the stocks that country contributes to, and each SC repository feeds the SA repository of its stock:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR

DK["NE-DK"] --> SC["SC-cod.27.347d"]
SE["NE-SE"] --> SC
NO["NE-NO"] --> SC
UK["NE-UK"] --> SC

SC --> SA["SA-cod.27.347d"]
```

An NE repository can contribute to many SC repositories, one for each stock its country provides data for. Which NE repositories contribute to each SC repository is maintained in a contributor table, for example:

| NE repository | SC repository |
|---------------|---------------|
| NE-DK | SC-cod.27.347d |
| NE-SE | SC-cod.27.347d |
| NE-NO | SC-cod.27.347d |
| NE-UK | SC-cod.27.347d |

This connection, from an NE repository to an SC repository, is what gives WG and ADG members read access to NE repositories: a member who can read the SC repository of a stock can also read the NE repositories that contribute to it.

## Business access model

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR

User --> STAFF["ICES staff"]
User --> ACOM
User --> ADG
User --> WG

STAFF --> ALL["All Repositories"]
ACOM --> ALL

ADG --> Stock
WG --> Stock

Stock --> SC["SC Repository"]
Stock --> SA["SA Repository"]

NE["NE Repository"] -->|"Contributes Data"| SC
SC -->|"Feeds"| SA

ADG -->|"Read"| SC
ADG -->|"Read"| SA
ADG -->|"Read Contributing"| NE

WG -->|"Read"| SC
WG -->|"Read"| SA
WG -->|"Read Contributing"| NE

User -->|"SC Claim"| SC
User -->|"SA Claim"| SA
User -->|"NE Claim"| NE
```

## Source systems

The systems of record used to determine authorization:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR

RDBES["RDBES"]
SID["SID"]
CRM["CRM"]
CT["Contributor Table"]
HR["Identity / HR Source"]

RDBES -->|"NE Claims
User ↔ Country"| AUTH

SID -->|"SC Claims
User ↔ Stock"| AUTH
SID -->|"SA Claims
User ↔ Stock"| AUTH
SID -->|"WG ↔ Stock"| AUTH
SID -->|"ADG ↔ Stock"| AUTH

CRM -->|"User ↔ WG"| AUTH
CRM -->|"User ↔ ADG"| AUTH
CRM -->|"ACOM Membership"| AUTH

CT -->|"NE → SC Contributions"| AUTH
HR -->|"ICES Staff Membership"| AUTH

AUTH["Authorization Engine"]
```

## Authorization evaluation

How access to a repository is evaluated. Write claims are checked first, so that ICES staff and ACOM members who also hold a claim get write access, not only read access.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD

A["User Requests Repository"]

A --> C{"Write Claim Match?"}

C -->|NE=Country| WRITE["Write Allowed"]
C -->|SC=Stock| WRITE
C -->|SA=Stock| WRITE

C -->|No Match| B{"ICES Staff or ACOM?"}

B -->|Yes| READ["Read Allowed"]

B -->|No| D{"WG or ADG Member?"}

D -->|No| DENY["Access Denied"]

D -->|Yes| E{"Repository Type?"}

E -->|"SC or SA, stock owned by WG/ADG"| READ
E -->|"NE, contributes to SC of owned stock"| READ
E -->|Otherwise| DENY
```

## Access rules summary

| Source | Access |
|--------|--------|
| ICES staff | Read all repositories |
| ACOM member | Read all repositories |
| ADG member | Read SC repositories for ADG stocks |
| ADG member | Read SA repositories for ADG stocks |
| ADG member | Read NE repositories contributing to the SC repositories of ADG stocks |
| WG member | Read SC repositories for WG stocks |
| WG member | Read SA repositories for WG stocks |
| WG member | Read NE repositories contributing to the SC repositories of WG stocks |
| NE claim | Write matching NE repositories |
| SC claim | Write matching SC repositories |
| SA claim | Write matching SA repositories |

## Data relationships

The authorization model depends on the following maintained relationships:

```text
User
 ├─ NE Claim (RDBES)
 ├─ SC Claim (SID)
 ├─ SA Claim (SID)
 ├─ WG Membership (CRM)
 ├─ ADG Membership (CRM)
 ├─ ACOM Membership (CRM)
 └─ ICES Staff Membership (Identity / HR Source)

WG ──────────────► Stock          (SID)

ADG ─────────────► Stock          (SID)

Stock ───────────► SC Repository

Stock ───────────► SA Repository

NE Repository ───► SC Repository  (Contributor Table)

SC Repository ───► SA Repository
```
